newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan stock rally loses steam in late trade.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan stock rally loses steam in late trade.

text.p: Taiwan share prices turned mixed in late trade on Tuesday, losing much of their early gains in the face of technical and psychological pressure and market-cooling moves by the central bank, brokers said.
With 50 minutes left, at 0310 GMT, the benchmark stock index was up just 3.91 points or 0.04 percent at 9,597.45, well off its dizzy intraday high of 9,714.78.
Turnover was heavy at T$180.1 billion.
"The pressure was too strong. Also, the central bank's moves to mop up excess funds were obvious," Nomura Securities analyst Amy Huang said.
She said electronics had risen strongly for some time and some investors were succumbing to a temptation to take profits.
Investors also were concerned about the central bank's moves to tighten banking-system liquidity to prevent excessive funds from flowing into the red-hot stock, she said.
The central bank has repeated issued negotiable certificates of desposit to tighten market liquidity. On Tuesday, it said it was issuing T$8 billion worth of NCDs.
Central bank deputy governor Hsu Chia-tung hinted on Monday that the bank would take action if the stock rally was seen as becoming too speculative.
With the exception of the bullish electronics sector, which has carried the market in recent weeks, most sectors were down.
Motherboard giant Asustek had risen the daily seven percent limit to T$463, rising T$30. Chipmaker Winbond was nearly limit-up, rising T$3 to T$72.5. Computer giant Acer Inc was up T$1 to T$99.
Brokers said new credit-buying limits, activated once the index hit 9,600 under long-established rules, had slowed the rally, with buying interest dissipating above that level.
